title: Banana Bread
subtitle: a moist, one-bowl loaf made with very ripe bananas
excerpt: The riper the bananas, the better the banana bread. Completely black bananas are perfect -- they are sweeter, more intense, and mash to a smooth paste. This is a forgiving loaf that comes together in minutes.
sourceNotes: Quick breads made with overripe bananas became popular in the US during the 1930s and have been widely adopted in British home baking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Slice and freeze. Defrost at room temperature or toast from frozen.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps well for 3 to 4 days wrapped in foil. Improves on the second day.

content.text: Mash the bananas thoroughly with a fork until no large lumps remain. A few small pieces are fine but the batter should be mostly smooth. Do not use a blender -- hand mashing gives the right texture. Mix the batter by hand; over-mixing by machine can make the loaf tough.

items.prepNote: use 3 very ripe bananas, mashed (about 280g peeled weight)

content.text: Heat the oven to 180C. Grease and line a 900g loaf tin.
Mash the ripe bananas in a large bowl. Add the melted butter, sugar, beaten eggs, vanilla, and cinnamon. Stir to combine.
Add the flour, baking powder, and bicarbonate of soda. Fold together until just combined. Stop as soon as you can no longer see dry flour -- do not over-mix.
Pour into the prepared tin. Bake for 55 to 60 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. If the top is browning too quickly, lay a sheet of foil loosely over the tin.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack. Leave for at least 30 minutes before slicing.

items.symptom: Loaf is gummy in the centre
items.cause: Under-baked. Banana bread takes longer than expected because the wet batter is dense.
items.fix: Test with a skewer deep in the centre. If it comes out wet, give it 10 more minutes. Cover the top with foil if it is already dark.
The bananas must be very ripe -- deep brown or black skins. Yellow or slightly speckled bananas will give a pale, starchy result.

content.text: Banana bread is a product of American quick bread traditions and became widely popular in Britain from the 1990s onwards, partly through cafe culture. It is one of the most searched-for baking recipes online. It is the thing people make when they have bananas going black on the counter, and the result always surprises anyone who expects it to taste like effort.
